signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Disruption
signals.text: NOK leads the weekly G10 currency strength scorecard at +1.344% across 2 pairs, while USD anchors the bottom at −0.619% across 9 pairs, generating an outsized bilateral spread of 1.963%. The divergence is accelerated by Strait of Hormuz maritime disruption headlines after an Iranian naval mine blast, driving energy supply-risk premiums into crude exporters. Norges Bank policy rate at 4.5% versus Fed at 4.00% delivers a +50bp policy carry advantage to NOK, further reinforced by Norway's ESI outperformance at +17.2 compared to USD's +10.5. Technical positioning confirms the cross-pair momentum, with USD/NOK closing at 9.414, breaking cleanly below its SMA20 (9.530), SMA50 (9.423), and SMA200 (9.532) cluster. Retail positioning shows an absolute extreme with 100% long exposure in USD/NOK, setting up a forced capitulation squeeze into the technical breakdown. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/USD; energy supply disruption and policy spread favor continued divergence. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 5 Nov. Risk: De-escalation in the Persian Gulf softens crude prices and closes the bilateral gap below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.83, holding above its SMA20 at 157.91 and SMA50 at 157.71 while capped beneath the 200-day moving average at 158.55. Fed policy at 4.00% versus BoJ at 1.25% yields a 275bp policy spread, complemented by an overnight SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential of +266bp supporting USD long holds. However, 25-delta risk reversals print at −1.91 for the 1-month tenor, reflecting aggressive institutional demand for JPY call protection against intervention or equity contagion. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net short JPY position of −37,820 contracts at the 88th percentile of their 52-week range, indicating carry positioning remains crowded despite a −7,441 contract WoW reduction. With VIX at 20.0 indicating normal volatility, broad safe-haven flight is contained, leaving the downside skew primarily reflective of policy barrier sensitivity near 160.00. Trade bias: Range USD/JPY; carry persistence competes with heavy downside option hedging. Catalyst: Japan Adjusted Trade Balance at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A breach above 160.00 prompts direct MoF intervention, triggering disorderly long covering.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Spec Short + Vol Hedging Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1225, pinned below its SMA20 at 1.1287, SMA50 at 1.1472, and SMA200 at 1.1588. Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp rate spread favoring USD, while the SOFR-€STR OIS basis trades at +145bp. CFTC data shows institutional speculative positioning heavily compressed, with Leveraged Funds net short −92,833 contracts at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of −1.78, following a −8,058 contract WoW drop. In options, 1-month ATM implied volatility runs at 6.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.0% that signals defensive downside hedging. While German unemployment change posted a +2.96σ adverse shock, the crowded speculative short profile leaves the pair vulnerable to sharp short-covering bounces on any macroeconomic surprise. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; structural carry deficit weighs against crowded short positioning. Catalyst: Germany ZEW Economic Sentiment at 09:05 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds cover short positions aggressively, forcing a technical reclaim above the SMA20 at 1.1287.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Energy Terms of Trade vs Inflation Event Risk
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4122, testing immediate support below the SMA20 at 1.4188 while remaining positioned above the SMA50 at 1.3997 and SMA200 at 1.3876. The Fed-BoC policy differential stands at 175bp with Fed at 4.00% and BoC at 2.25%, generating a +162bp SOFR-CORRA OIS carry buffer for the US dollar. WTI crude oil at $97.9/bbl amidst Persian Gulf tanker transit risks provides CAD terms-of-trade backing, aligning with CAD's +0.637% 1-week gain across G10 peers. Leveraged Funds hold CAD net short at −89,659 contracts (15th percentile, z-score −1.32), while retail traders register an extreme 86% short exposure on USD/CAD, establishing conflicting positioning dynamics. The 2-year sovereign yield spread moved −7bp over 5 days to −162bp against Canada, maintaining USD monetary advantage ahead of domestic price pressures. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; elevated energy prices pressure the carry floor ahead of key inflation data. Catalyst: Canada Core CPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Canadian Core CPI prints below the 2.1% forecast, reviving BoC dovish easing expectations.
